# Teme developer handbook

Guides for people and agents who build Teme plugins and themes. Reference under docs/reference/ is generated; these pages are written and tested against the code.

- [Plugin or theme?](start/plugin-or-theme.md): Which package you need — a plugin that adds behavior, or a theme that draws the public site.
- [Your first plugin](start/first-plugin.md): From an empty folder to an enabled plugin that listens to a hook.
- [Your first theme](start/first-theme.md): A theme with an index template and a single template, from the handbook example.
- [Set up a development site](start/development-site.md): One local Teme site that loads every plugin and theme you are building, straight from their own folders.
- [The manifest](concepts/manifest.md): How to write teme-plugin.json and teme-theme.json, and where the key tables live.
- [Hooks](concepts/hooks.md): The five verbs, the after-commit rule, capabilities, the Since version and requires.teme, and where the generated hook list lives.
- [Operations](concepts/operations.md): Every change goes through an Operation; what a plugin may and may not touch.
- [Code standards for plugins and themes](start/code-standards.md): What Teme requires of a plugin's or theme's code, what it only recommends, and where Teme's own coding standards are.
- [Testing a plugin or theme](testing.md): How to test a plugin or theme with Pest and Teme’s fixture helpers.
- [Plugin settings and secrets](plugins/settings.md): How a plugin declares its settings screen in the manifest, reads its values, keeps API keys as secrets, and adds a Tools link.
- [Regions, site code and featured posts](themes/regions.md): How a theme sets aside regions for the site's own content, where an administrator's own HTML goes, and how to draw pinned posts on the latest posts page.
- [Rules for plugins and themes](rules/plugins-and-themes.md): The rules every plugin and theme lives by, both the ones Teme enforces and the ones authors must keep because Teme cannot check them.
- [For agents](for-agents.md): How agents should read this handbook and llms.txt, choose a plugin's capabilities, and write an AGENTS.md for it.
- [Plugins writing content](plugins/content-write.md): How a plugin with content.write creates and changes items through Operations, with their slugs, credits and language versions, always for a named person.
- [Reading content](plugins/content-read.md): How a plugin with content.read lists the site's published items a page at a time, and reads an item's draft for the person its work acts for.
- [Jobs and schedules](plugins/jobs.md): Who a plugin's background job acts for, and every limit a job's run works within.
- [Public routes](plugins/public-routes.md): How a plugin will register routes reachable without signing in.
- [The plugin import socket](plugins/import.md): How a plugin will take part in site import.
- [Content inside articles](plugins/insertions.md): How a plugin with content.insert places markup between an article's blocks, such as ads, and what core cleans, caps and leaves out.
- [The fediverse](plugins/fediverse.md): What core does on the fediverse by itself, and the sockets a plugin can use to hear activities, handle them, change what is sent, and send its own.
- [List columns](plugins/list-columns.md): How a plugin adds a column to the admin's content lists.
- [Languages in a theme](themes/languages.md): What a multilingual site gives a theme, from the page's language and direction, its other language versions, the language switcher, and the theme's own words.
- [The management API](outside/management-api.md): For a service outside the site, not a plugin, with keys and abilities, the endpoints, the problems it answers, and its limits.
